summary: The paper proposes LayerBudget, an online training-free allocator that jointly assigns a per-layer token retention count n_l and a per-layer KV bit-width b_l in {4,8,16} under a global byte budget, using a greedy marginal-gain (delta-Q/delta-M) heuristic over a hand-built quality model Q = coverage(n_l; Gini) x fidelity(b_l) x importance(l). Secondary contributions are mean-fill for evicted KV positions and an empirical 'inverted importance' (protect early layers) default derived from leave-one-out probes. The evaluation grid is genuinely large: 7 models (7B-72B, MHA and GQA), 17 reimplemented baselines, 4 compression ratios, WikiText-2 PPL plus MMLU / GSM8K / NIAH / LongBench / RULER, 16K-32K long context, and a vLLM block-manager path. As an empiricist I care most about whether that grid actually establishes the headline claim, and it does not. Against the fairest strong baseline in the paper's own tables -- KIVI at INT4 -- LayerBudget wins 8 of 28 model x CR PPL cells (all at 2-3x, by 0.01-0.02, well inside the paper's own stated cross-chunk noise), ties 12, and loses 8 (every 6x cell and both 4x cells on Mistral-7B and Llama-2-13B). KIVI's row is numerically constant across all four CR columns, i.e. it is a single INT4 operating point run at roughly half LayerBudget's byte budget in the 2x column and never re-run at INT2 in the 6x column where LayerBudget fails -- so the comparison is unmatched in both directions and the one direction the authors could have fixed (KIVI-INT2 at 6x, cited in their own related work) is missing. The paper's own component ablation (Table A1) shows the joint allocator never strictly beats quant-only in any measured cell (1.00 vs 1.00, 1.02 vs 1.02 at 3x; 3.23 vs 1.00 and 45.09 vs 1.01 at 6x, i.e. joint loses), and the INT8 rung is worth 0.00-0.01 PPL (A3, {4,16} vs {4,8,16}). The single component with a large isolated effect is mean-fill, which is billed third and which the authors themselves show is matched by median-fill and random-fill. On top of that, the measurement layer has multiple internal contradictions I verified by recomputation: delta-F(4->8) is stated as 0.0035 in Section 3.5 but is 0.0224 from the paper's own calibration table; the memory-savings table reports 24.3%/71.2%/42.9% savings for three models all at nominal CR=2x (effective 1.32x/3.47x/1.76x), directly contradicting the Byte-CR appendix's claim that effective CR matches nominal within +/-0.05; Llama-3.1-8B and Mistral-7B are given base KV sizes of 189 MB and 95 MB despite identical KV geometry (32L, 8 KV heads, d=128); and the allocator's own cost projection ignores the O(L) inner scan in its own pseudocode (10 ms should be ~800 ms). Several baselines are implausible (SnapKV at 27.1-33.4% MMLU, near the 25% chance floor, on short prompts at 2-4x) and the LongBench evaluation returns 0.040-0.056 for Full KV, which means that harness is broken, not that LayerBudget matches Full KV. The fatal-flaw gate (a) is triggered: the method ties or loses to the strongest fair baseline on the metric that matters, and no end-to-end systems benefit is demonstrated to compensate (measured speedup < 1x, TPOT +2.6% to +12.2%, prefill profiling +61-109%).
strengths: The empirical grid is unusually wide for this area and is the paper's real asset: 7 models from 7B to 72B covering both MHA and GQA, 4 compression ratios, 17 baselines behind one interface, six evaluation surfaces (WikiText-2 PPL, MMLU 1140q, GSM8K 200q, NIAH, LongBench-16, RULER), 16K/32K long context, and a vLLM PagedAttention integration with 16-token block rounding. Most submissions in KV-cache compression report one model family and PPL plus LongBench; this one at least attempts breadth, and the 72B point (Qwen2.5-72B, 1.004 at 4x) is a real scaling data point few papers have.

The architecture-dependence result for eviction sensitivity is a genuine, well-instrumented negative finding with value beyond this paper. The same leave-one-out probe run on three models gives three different answers (Mistral-7B early-bottleneck; Llama-2-13B late-bottleneck, +0.093 on layers 26-39 vs +0.030 on layers 0-12; Qwen2.5-14B flat, +0.039 vs +0.038). Much of the per-layer-importance literature implicitly assumes a universal direction, and this probe is cheap (5 prompts, <1 min/model) and directly falsifies that assumption.

The mean-fill ablation is the cleanest experiment in the paper: it isolates one intervention, measures it on two models with two metrics (logits KL 0.249 -> 0.009 on Mistral-7B, 0.6696 -> 0.0636 on Llama-2-7B; PPL ratio 45.09 -> 1.13 on Llama-2-7B at 6x), and includes the right control (median-fill and random-fill with matched mean/std give comparable results), which correctly identifies first-moment preservation rather than the mean specifically as the operative mechanism.

The online profiling signal is designed for deployability and its cost is measured rather than assumed. Using only the last attention row per layer is O(S) rather than O(S^2), and the overhead table reports prefill, attention overhead, Gini and allocation separately across S = 256/512/1024 on two models, with the honest disclosure that the 100-513 ms figure is the whole pipeline and not the allocator alone.

Reporting practice on losses is above the norm for this literature: the 6x collapse, the LayerBudget-KV NIAH drop to 26.7%, MoE-nD winning the Mistral 6x cell, the < 1x measured speedup, the Llama-2-13B 1.56 at 6x, and the MiniKV 11.92x blow-up are all in the tables rather than omitted. This makes the paper auditable, which is why I was able to check it -- though per the gate, disclosure does not repair the underlying results.
weaknesses: FATAL (gate a): LayerBudget does not beat the fairest strong baseline on the metric that matters. Tabulating the paper's own two PPL tables across 7 models x 4 CRs (28 cells) against KIVI: LayerBudget wins 8 cells (Llama-2-7B/Mistral/Llama-3.1/Qwen3/Llama-2-13B/Qwen2.5-14B at 2x, Llama-2-13B at 3x) by margins of 0.01-0.02; ties 12; and loses 8 (every 6x cell on all seven models, Mistral-7B at 4x, Llama-2-13B at 4x with 1.11 vs 1.02). The winning margins are smaller than the paper's own stated noise (PPL std ~2.3 across the 6 WikiText-2 chunks), and the paper itself concedes 'LayerBudget matches KIVI's PPL within sampling noise at 2-3x'. On MMLU, KIVI equals or beats LayerBudget on 4 of 5 models (47.7=47.7, 63.7 vs 64.1, 60.1=60.1, 72.7 vs 72.6, 76.6 vs 76.1). On LongBench the two are within 0.003 of each other and of Full KV. On GSM8K the ordering flips per model and LayerBudget beats Full KV on 3 of 4 models, so the metric does not discriminate. The entire differentiating evidence over KIVI reduces to a single NIAH cell (Llama-2-7B, 100 vs 93.3 at n=15-30, i.e. one to two needles) plus one Mistral cell where both methods score 73.3. Fix: run a memory-matched sweep in which KIVI is given exactly LayerBudget's byte budget at each CR and is allowed the INT2 mode the paper's own related work attributes to it, and report paired bootstrap CIs. If LayerBudget does not separate from KIVI there, the contribution claim must be restated as 'matches quantization while additionally reducing token count', and then the token-count reduction must be shown to buy something measurable (see next item).

The token-count reduction -- the only axis on which LayerBudget differs from KIVI -- is never shown to produce a systems benefit, which removes the fallback justification for the tie. The memory-savings table's own footnote states 'Speedup < 1x due to compression overhead'; the TPOT table shows +2.6% to +12.2% decode overhead; the profiling table shows the full pipeline adding 61-109% to prefill. No throughput (tokens/s), no maximum batch size at fixed VRAM, no TTFT, no peak-memory-at-128K, and no serving-level experiment appears anywhere. The paper's motivation (Llama-2-70B at 8K needs >40 GB) is a serving-capacity argument that is never closed. Fix: report tokens/s and max concurrent sequences at fixed GPU memory for LayerBudget vs KIVI vs Full KV, or drop the systems framing.

The paper's own component ablation contradicts its primary contribution claim, and the caption misstates its own table. Table A1 gives Joint vs Quant-only as 1.00 vs 1.00 (Mistral 3x), 1.02 vs 1.02 (Llama-2 3x), 3.23 vs 1.00 (Mistral 6x) and 45.09 vs 1.01 (Llama-2 6x): the joint allocator never strictly wins and loses badly at 6x, yet the caption asserts 'The joint approach exceeds quant-only at 3x'. On Llama-2-7B at 3x, eviction-only (1.00) also beats joint (1.02). Table A3 shows the INT8 rung is worth at most 0.01 PPL ({4,16} vs {4,8,16}: 1.01/1.00 at Mistral 3x, identical in all other cells) even though 'exhausts INT4/INT8 headroom' is a headline mechanism in the abstract. Fix: either produce a memory-matched A1 in which quant-only is forced to the same byte budget at 6x (with INT2/INT3), which is the comparison the appendix prose says is needed but never runs, or demote 'joint (n_l,b_l) allocation' from the first contribution.

Baseline validity is not established, and at least two baselines are implausible enough to invalidate the 'ranks 1st' claim. SnapKV scores 27.1 / 29.6 / 29.4 / 33.4 / 41.2 on MMLU across five models -- essentially the 25% chance floor -- at CR=2-4x on MMLU's short prompts, where any correct heavy-hitter implementation should be near-lossless because there is barely anything to evict. H2O is defended in a table caption but SnapKV is not defended at all. MiniKV registers 11.92x on Mistral at 6x, flagged 'not a typo'. All 17 baselines are the authors' own reimplementations; the de-facto community harness (NVIDIA KVPress, which ships 30+ methods, a public leaderboard, and built-in PerLayerCompressionPress / QuantizedCache) is never mentioned or used. Fix: reproduce at least H2O, SnapKV, PyramidKV and KIVI numbers inside KVPress at a matched budget and show they land within a stated tolerance of the published numbers, before claiming a rank over them.

The LongBench experiment is broken and cannot support the claim it is used for. Full KV scores 0.056 / 0.040 / 0.050 (mean F1/ROUGE-L over 16 English tasks) on Mistral-7B / Llama-3.1-8B / Llama-2-7B. Published LongBench scores for these models are roughly an order of magnitude higher; a Full-KV score of 0.05 means the generation or scoring path is producing near-worthless output before any compression is applied, so 'LayerBudget matches Full KV on all models' is a statement about a broken harness. The H2O anomaly (0.097 > Full KV 0.050, explained as 'degenerate repetition inflating F1') is a second symptom of the same problem. Relatedly, Full KV NIAH on Mistral-7B is 86.7% at only 4096 tokens, where an uncompressed Mistral-7B should be at or near 100%, indicating the NIAH harness is also misconfigured. Fix: debug both harnesses until Full KV reproduces published reference values, then re-run; and move to LongBench-v2 / RULER at multiple lengths, which is what this community now expects.

Recomputation defect: the fidelity constants used by the solver contradict the paper's own calibration table. Section 3.5 justifies diminishing returns with 'delta-F(4->8) = 0.0035 > delta-F(8->16) = 0.0001'. From the per-model calibration appendix, mean F(8) = 0.9998 and mean F(4) = 0.9774, so delta-F(4->8) = 0.0224 -- 6.4x the stated value -- and delta-F(8->16) = 0.0002. Section 3.2 ('the ~2% F(4) gap') and Appendix C ('F(8) and F(4) differ by only 0.02') both agree with 0.0224, so 0.0035 is the outlier. Since delta-Q/delta-M ranking is what drives every allocation decision, a 6x error in the dominant fidelity increment is not cosmetic: it changes when the allocator prefers a bit-upgrade over a token-add. The appendix mean F(4) also recomputes to 0.9774, not the 0.976 stated in Section 3.2. Fix: state which constant the released code uses, and re-run the main table if it is 0.0035.

Recomputation defect: the allocator complexity/latency projection omits the inner loop in its own pseudocode. Section 3.4 claims O(L * S/delta_n) iterations, giving 80*32768/8 = 327,680 for Qwen2.5-72B at 32K and '~10 ms at ~30 ns/iteration'. But Algorithm 1 places a FOR over every layer and both actions inside the WHILE, so the work is O(L^2 * S/delta_n) = 80 * 327,680 ~= 26.2M evaluations, i.e. ~800 ms at the same 30 ns -- comparable to a full prefill, not 'small relative to a single decode step'. No priority-queue or incremental-argmax optimization is described. Fix: either present the amortized data structure that makes the claim true, or measure the allocator at S=32K on the 72B model instead of extrapolating.

The compression ratio is not a single well-defined quantity, and the paper's own reconciliation appendix is falsified by its own tables. (i) The memory-savings table reports 24.3% / 71.2% / 42.9% savings for Llama-2-7B / Llama-3.1-8B / Mistral-7B all at nominal CR=2x, i.e. effective 1.32x / 3.47x / 1.76x -- a 2.6x spread across models at one nominal setting, versus the Byte-CR appendix's claim that 'every method's effective CR matches its nominal CR within +/-0.05'. (ii) The appendix says the allocator-side 2x inflation 'is fixed across methods', but in the nominal-6x memory table H2O is 39296/6528 = 6.02x (no inflation at all), KIVI 3.93x, Ada-KV 8.91x and LayerBudget 3.04x -- LayerBudget is spending 2.0x the bytes of H2O and 1.3x the bytes of KIVI at the same nominal CR, so that table's PPL comparison is not memory-matched in LayerBudget's disfavour. (iii) The abstract claims a 'memory-matched comparison' whose supporting appendix is only cited, never shown. Fix: regenerate every table under mean_memory_bytes before submission (the paper defers this to camera-ready), and delete the memory-matched claim until the table exists.

Arithmetic/geometry error in the memory table undermines confidence in all reported byte counts. Llama-3.1-8B and Mistral-7B have identical KV geometry (32 layers, 8 KV heads, head_dim 128), so their FP16 base KV at 512 tokens must be identical (2*32*512*8*128*2 bytes = 67.1 MB). The table reports 189 MB and 95 MB -- differing by exactly 2x, and both above the analytic value. Llama-2-7B (32L, 32H, 128) should be exactly 4x Mistral's; the reported 287/95 = 3.02x. Fix: recompute base KV analytically per model and reconcile with the instrumented numbers.

The headline abstract number is false as written by the paper's own table. 'LayerBudget achieves PPL ratio <= 1.03 at 4x on seven models from 7B to 72B' -- the large-model table gives Llama-2-13B at 4x as 1.11 (and 1.56 at 6x). The parenthetical ('<= 1.01 on 13B-72B at GQA') silently excludes the one MHA model in that range that violates the claim. Separately, the main results table is computed with mean-fill, while Section 4.3 calls zero-fill 'the practical deployment setting'; in that deployment setting Llama-2-7B is 1.17 at 4x and 45.09 at 6x. So the headline operating envelope is reported in a configuration the authors themselves say is not the deployment one. Fix: restate the abstract as '<= 1.03 at 4x on the GQA models; 1.11 on Llama-2-13B (MHA)', and make zero-fill the primary table if it is the deployment setting.

Statistical rigour is insufficient for the size of the claimed effects. Every PPL number comes from 6 WikiText-2 chunks with an acknowledged cross-chunk std of ~2.3 PPL, yet differences of 0.01-0.03 in PPL ratio carry the entire argument, and no table reports a confidence interval or a paired test (one truncated parenthetical mentions a paired bootstrap but no interval is given anywhere). NIAH cells are n=15-30 (all values are multiples of 1/15 or 1/30), so '100 vs 93.3' is one to two needles; GSM8K is n=200 with Full KV at 5.5% on Llama-2-7B and LayerBudget exceeding Full KV on 3 of 4 models; RULER on the 72B model improves from 98 at 2x to 100 at 4x, which is a noise signature. Fix: report paired bootstrap CIs on every headline comparison, increase WikiText-2 chunks to at least 50, and increase NIAH to the standard depth x length grid.

The claimed contribution is compressed into an operating envelope (2-4x) that quantization alone already covers, while the field's current bar is much higher. INT4 quantization gives ~4x by itself, and the paper's own signal-crossover ablation says that below 3.5x 'no tokens are evicted' and 'all signal variants are equivalent' -- i.e. in most of the claimed envelope LayerBudget reduces to KIVI. Above 4x it degrades (Mistral 1.25, Llama-2-13B 1.56 at 6x), and the LayerBudget-KV variant that fixes PPL at 6x collapses NIAH to 26.7%. Concurrent and published 2026 work operates at 14-20x (MoE-nD, STAR-KV, KVTC) or <5% cache retention (ThinKV). The paper never evaluates against RDKV, HqeKV, ThinKV, KVTC, STAR-KV or DefensiveKV, and its only two joint-method comparisons (MoE-nD, xKV) are the authors' own reimplementations of unreleased artifacts that both conveniently lose. Fix: at minimum reproduce one public joint quant+eviction method (HqeKV has public code) at matched budget, and report the effective-bits-per-token currency the field now uses.

The quality model that the whole method optimizes is never validated against quality. Q = C x F x w is summed over layers and maximized, but only C is checked (3.1% MAE against captured attention mass on one model), F is a cosine similarity never mapped to any quality metric, and w is a hand-set sigmoid (k=5, tau=0.3, neither ablated) whose direction the paper's own LOO probe shows is wrong for Llama-2-13B. There is no experiment correlating the optimized objective Sum_l Q with measured PPL or task accuracy, and no experiment showing greedy's allocation beats a random or uniform allocation at equal bytes under the same fill strategy. The claim that 'greedy achieves 118-119%' of something is truncated in the submitted text and its reference point is never identified; if the reference is the MCKP optimum, exceeding 100% is impossible. Fix: add a scatter of predicted Sum_l Q against measured PPL ratio across many allocations, and name the 118-119% denominator.

The recommended deployment configuration is never evaluated end to end. The method section says a per-architecture importance direction set by a 5-prompt LOO probe 'is the recommended deployment recipe' and 'would tighten the Llama-2-13B 6x ratio (currently 1.56)', but no table anywhere reports results under that recipe -- every reported number uses the Mistral-tuned inverted default. A recommended configuration with zero measured results is an unsupported contribution. Fix: add the per-architecture-direction row to the large-model table.

Format/style items that are desk-reject risks under the stated NeurIPS rules: the 18-column main results table is wrapped in \resizebox{\textwidth}{!}{...} on top of \small and \tabcolsep=2pt, which scales the font well below the template size (the handbook names decreasing font sizes as a desk-reject trigger); negative \vspace of -0.2in / -0.1in / -0.05in is used around figures and tables to reclaim space. In the provided source, the Analysis section header is unclosed, one table environment is written as \begin{table[t], a \textbf{Downstream accuracy. group is unclosed, the sentence 'On LongBench (16 English tasks, Table~[REF]' ends mid-clause, and the Limitations list appears with no section heading -- as provided this source would not compile. Fix: remove resizebox and negative vspace (split the table instead), and verify a clean compile and the 9-page content limit.
questions: Memory-matched KIVI: what is KIVI's PPL, MMLU and NIAH when it is given exactly LayerBudget's measured mean_memory_bytes at each nominal CR (not the single INT4 point that produces the constant 1.01/1.02 row), and what is KIVI-INT2 at 6x, the operating point your own related work says KIVI supports and the one where LayerBudget degrades to 1.25 (Mistral) / 1.56 (Llama-2-13B)? Please report paired bootstrap CIs. This single experiment decides whether the paper has a contribution over quantization.

Which delta-F(4->8) does the released allocator actually use, 0.0035 (Section 3.5) or the 0.0224 implied by your calibration table and by Appendix C's 'differ by only 0.02'? If the code uses 0.0035, does the main table change when it is corrected, given that this increment is what makes bit-upgrades outrank token-adds?

How is mean-fill realized in memory at inference time? If the S - n_l evicted positions are materialized so they can participate in attention, the byte savings you report are not realized; if a single mean vector is broadcast, which attention kernel does that, and is that path the one used to produce the memory-savings and TPOT tables? Relatedly, why is zero-fill called 'the practical deployment setting' if mean-fill is deployable, and why are the headline results reported under mean-fill?

Please reconcile the memory-savings table with the Byte-CR appendix: at nominal CR=2x you report 24.3% (Llama-2-7B), 71.2% (Llama-3.1-8B) and 42.9% (Mistral-7B) savings, i.e. effective 1.32x, 3.47x and 1.76x, against the appendix's claim of nominal-vs-effective agreement within +/-0.05 over 1,779 checkpoints. Separately, why do Llama-3.1-8B and Mistral-7B have base KV of 189 MB and 95 MB at 512 tokens when both are 32 layers x 8 KV heads x d=128 (analytically 67.1 MB)?

SnapKV scores 27.1-41.2 on MMLU at CR=2-4x, essentially chance, on prompts short enough that little eviction should occur. Can you show your SnapKV (and H2O, PyramidKV, Ada-KV) reproducing their published numbers on at least one shared benchmark configuration, ideally inside NVIDIA KVPress? Without that, 'ranks 1st among 17 baselines' is not supportable.

Full KV scores 0.040-0.056 on LongBench-16 and 86.7% on 4K NIAH for Mistral-7B. Both are far below what these uncompressed models achieve. What is the harness bug, and does 'LayerBudget matches Full KV on LongBench' survive a fixed harness (and on LongBench-v2 / RULER at 4K-32K rather than v1)?

Table A1 shows the joint allocator tying quant-only at 3x on both models and losing to it at 6x, and Table A3 shows the INT8 rung worth <= 0.01 PPL. What experiment isolates a positive marginal effect of the joint (n_l,b_l) allocation itself -- as opposed to mean-fill and INT4 quantization -- at equal bytes? If none exists, would you agree the contribution ordering in the abstract should be inverted?

The 'recommended deployment recipe' (per-architecture importance direction from a 5-prompt LOO probe) has no end-to-end numbers anywhere. What are the full PPL / NIAH / MMLU results under that recipe on Llama-2-13B and Qwen2.5-14B?

probe_answers.answer: Five plausible alternatives. (1) KIVI / uniform INT4 quantization (Sec 2, main results table): compared head-to-head -- and it wins or ties. Across the 28 model x CR PPL cells in the main and large-model tables, LayerBudget wins 8 (all 2x-3x, margins 0.01-0.02), ties 12, loses 8 (all 4x-6x). KIVI's row is numerically constant across all four CR columns, i.e. one INT4 operating point, so in the 2x column KIVI is running at roughly half LayerBudget's byte budget and still ties within noise; and at 6x KIVI cannot reach the budget at all, yet the INT2 mode the paper's own Section 2 attributes to KIVI is never run. The comparison is therefore unmatched in both directions and the fixable direction was not fixed. (2) StreamingLLM / 'keep sink + recent window' trivial baseline: present and beaten -- good, this is the right sanity baseline and the paper includes it. (3) Concurrent joint quant+eviction methods (MoE-nD, xKV): compared, but only as the authors' own reimplementations of artifacts that were not public, with an explicit caveat that divergence may be due to implementation gaps; both lose. Self-reimplemented private baselines that lose carry near-zero evidential weight. (4) Published 2026 joint / hybrid methods with public code or top-venue results -- RDKV (rate-distortion joint bit allocation, exactly this paper's formulation), HqeKV (ACL 2026 Findings, code public, hybrid quantization+eviction), ThinKV, KVTC (ICLR 2026), STAR-KV (ICML 2026 Spotlight), DefensiveKV / Layer-DefensiveKV (ICLR 2026), PolyKV: ignored entirely, not cited, not compared. HqeKV in particular has public code and is the direct competitor. (5) NVIDIA KVPress, the de-facto harness with 30+ methods, a public leaderboard and built-in PerLayerCompressionPress and QuantizedCache: never mentioned; every one of the 17 baselines is a private reimplementation. DEFECT: an obvious alternative (KIVI) is compared and is not beaten, and the closest public competitor (HqeKV) plus the standard harness are ignored.

Eleven. (1) 'CR' is overloaded four ways -- nominal CR, token-count CR, method-byte CR, and allocator-side CR -- and the Byte-CR appendix adds a fifth ('effective CR'); Section 4 concedes 'its byte budget at a given nominal CR may differ'. (2) 'LayerBudget' names the allocator, the full profiling+allocation+selection+fill pipeline, the HuggingFace DynamicCache subclass, and the vLLM block manager; the 1 ms vs 100-513 ms overhead discrepancy is entirely a consequence of this overloading. (3) Q(l,n_l,b_l) has no units and is never tied to any measurable quality; the objective sums it across layers with no argument for additivity or commensurability with PPL. (4) B, the memory budget, is never given units. (5) n_min = sink + recent: the sink and recent token counts are never numerically specified anywhere, so no allocation is reproducible. (6) g_l (Gini) is used in Eq. 3 before being defined in Sec 3.3, and the only reported Gini statistics (range 0.43-0.93, rho=0.194) are from TinyLlama-1.1B, a model that appears in no results table. (7) k=5 and tau=0.3 are stated without derivation, source, or ablation. (8) 'LB' appears as a method name in three tables and in the Key-findings bullets without ever being introduced as an abbreviation for LayerBudget. (9) The category codes 'Ph', 'Qt', 'Jt' and 'Cat.' in the main results table are never expanded in the caption or text. (10) 'fidelity' F(b) is defined operationally as a cosine similarity but used multiplicatively as a quality factor; the mapping from cosine 0.977 to any quality unit is never given. (11) 'mean_memory_bytes' and 'allocator-side accounting' are load-bearing for every memory claim but are defined only in an appendix, after the tables that depend on them. Also: the '118-119%' figure appears twice with its denominator never named. DEFECT.

Three recomputations, all failing. (A) FIDELITY INCREMENTS. Sec 3.5 states delta-F(4->8) = 0.0035 > delta-F(8->16) = 0.0001. From the per-model calibration table: mean F(8) = (0.9998+0.9997+0.9999+0.9997+0.9998+0.9999)/6 = 0.99980; mean F(4) = (0.9794+0.9758+0.9817+0.9683+0.9781+0.9810)/6 = 0.97738. So delta-F(4->8) = 0.99980 - 0.97738 = 0.02242 (6.4x the stated 0.0035) and delta-F(8->16) = 1.0000 - 0.99980 = 0.00020 (2x the stated 0.0001). Sec 3.2's '~2% F(4) gap' and Appendix C's 'differ by only 0.02' both corroborate 0.0224, so the constant used to justify diminishing returns -- and, since delta-Q/delta-M is the sole allocation rule, to decide when a bit-upgrade outranks a token-add -- is wrong by 6.4x in the paper. Sec 3.2's stated mean F(4) = 0.976 also recomputes to 0.9774. DOES NOT CHECK OUT. (B) ALLOCATOR LATENCY. Sec 3.4: '80 * 32768/8 ~= 327K iterations ... at ~30 ns per iteration this projects to ~10 ms'. 80*32768/8 = 327,680 and 327,680 * 30 ns = 9.83 ms, so the arithmetic is right but the complexity is wrong: Algorithm 1 puts a FOR over all L layers x 2 actions inside the WHILE, so total work is L * (L*S/delta_n) = 80 * 327,680 = 26.2M evaluations = 786 ms at the same 30 ns. Off by a factor of L = 80. No incremental-argmax or heap is described. DOES NOT CHECK OUT. (C) KV GEOMETRY. Memory-savings table at S=512, FP16: Mistral-7B (32L, 8 KV heads, d=128) analytic base KV = 2*32*512*8*128*2 B = 67.1 MB; Llama-3.1-8B has identical geometry so must equal it. Reported: 95 MB and 189 MB -- a 2x discrepancy between two architecturally identical caches. Llama-2-7B (32L, 32H, d=128) analytic = 268 MB, reported 287 MB, and 287/95 = 3.02x where the geometry demands exactly 4x. DOES NOT CHECK OUT. (Two claims that DO check out: mean-fill KL reduction (0.249-0.009)/0.249 = 96.4% and (0.6696-0.0636)/0.6696 = 90.5%.) DEFECT.

Four strawman/unfair-baseline findings, and the abstract's most favorable number is not the honest one. (1) The abstract headline 'At 32K context on Mistral-7B, H2O at 4x collapses (83x PPL) while LayerBudget maintains 1.009x' is a quantization-vs-eviction comparison dressed as method-vs-method: under the paper's byte-based CR, H2O at 4x must keep 25% of tokens at FP16 while LayerBudget may keep nearly all tokens at INT4. In the same table KIVI -- plain uniform INT4 -- scores 1.008, i.e. equal to LayerBudget. The honest reading of the paper's flagship long-context result is 'INT4 quantization solves this cell; our allocator adds nothing'. (2) The importance-direction ablation's headline gain ('60-94%') is measured against 'Sigmoid (late-high)', a deliberately inverted variant, not against the natural default. Against Flat (uniform) the gains are 1.010 -> 1.008 at 4x on Mistral (0.2%) and 1.067 -> 1.002 on Llama-2, i.e. essentially nil in the 2-4x envelope the paper claims as its operating regime. (3) SnapKV at 27.1-41.2 MMLU (chance = 25%) and MiniKV at 11.92x on Mistral 6x are not credible faithful implementations; H2O's collapse is defended in a caption, SnapKV's is not defended at all. (4) The MoE-nD and xKV rows are the authors' own reimplementations of non-public artifacts, with a written caveat that divergence may be 'implementation gaps'; both lose. (5) The abstract's 'PPL ratio <= 1.03 at 4x on seven models from 7B to 72B' is contradicted by the paper's own table (Llama-2-13B = 1.11 at 4x, 1.56 at 6x) and by the deployment (zero-fill) setting the paper itself names (Llama-2-7B = 1.17 at 4x). DEFECT.

Ten internal contradictions. (1) delta-F(4->8) = 0.0035 (Sec 3.5) vs 0.0224 from the calibration appendix, vs 'differ by only 0.02' (Appendix C), vs '~2% F(4) gap' (Sec 3.2). (2) Abstract '<= 1.03 at 4x on seven models' vs Llama-2-13B = 1.11 at 4x and 1.56 at 6x in the large-model table. (3) Byte-CR appendix: 'every method's effective CR matches its nominal CR within +/-0.05' vs the memory-savings table's 24.3% / 71.2% / 42.9% savings at one nominal CR=2x (effective 1.32x / 3.47x / 1.76x). (4) Byte-CR appendix: 'the 2x inflation is fixed across methods' vs the nominal-6x memory table where H2O = 6.02x (zero inflation), D2O = 6.04x, CAKE = 5.93x, Ada-KV = 8.91x, KIVI = 3.93x, LayerBudget = 3.04x -- the eviction methods show no inflation at all, so the inflation is method-dependent and LayerBudget is consuming 2.0x H2O's bytes in that table. (5) Table A1 caption 'The joint approach exceeds quant-only at 3x' vs its own cells (1.00 vs 1.00 Mistral; 1.02 vs 1.02 Llama-2 -- ties, and eviction-only 1.00 beats joint 1.02 on Llama-2). (6) 'Decode latency remains within 3-5%' and the TPOT caption 'adds 3-5%' vs +12.2% on Qwen2.5-14B in that same table. (7) Intro: 'Nearly all existing methods apply their strategy uniformly across layers' vs the Related Work paragraph listing PyramidKV, D2O, SqueezeAttention, CAKE, Ada-KV, EvolKV, LAVa, KVTuner and KVmix as per-layer or per-head methods. (8) Key finding 'GQA models are more robust. Mistral-7B shows less degradation than Llama-2-7B at matched compression' vs the same table at 6x where Mistral LayerBudget = 1.25 and Llama-2-7B = 1.17 (MHA better). (9) Main results are computed with mean-fill while Sec 4.3 calls zero-fill 'the practical deployment setting', so the headline envelope is not the deployment envelope. (10) Llama-3.1-8B base KV = 189 MB vs Mistral-7B = 95 MB despite identical KV geometry. DEFECT.

Yes, several passages read as machine-assisted or as transplanted rebuttal text rather than argument. (a) The token-eviction paragraph in Related Work is nine consecutive one-clause sentences of identical shape -- 'H2O retains attention heavy-hitters plus recent tokens. SnapKV uses observation-window voting. PyramidKV varies budget by layer depth with a fixed pyramid. D2O uses per-layer diversity-based allocation. SqueezeAttention classifies layers via residual cosine similarity...' -- a catalogue with uniform rhythm and no comparative argument. (b) Classic not-X-but-Y reframing of a losing result: 'The two design points are therefore best read as complementary operating regimes of the same framework rather than two competing solvers.' (c) Response-to-reviewer language left in a submission: 'we will update against their official code at camera-ready'; 'any divergence from the original authors' reported numbers should be attributed to (a) ... (b) ... (c) ...'; and an entire appendix ('Byte-CR Reconciliation') that functions as an erratum for a table the authors promise to regenerate later. (d) Unearned hedged generality: 'These approaches are orthogonal to per-layer joint allocation; LayerBudget could in principle be combined with HCAttention's heterogeneous compute path or PoD's cross-layer redundancy reduction' -- describes rather than argues, with no evidence. (e) Assertion-by-parallelism: 'Uniform compression either under-compresses easy layers or degrades critical layers.' (f) The MoE-nD discussion is a single ~500-word paragraph inside Related Work containing head-to-head numbers, a variant introduction, and a baselines caveat -- structurally a rebuttal pasted into a section that should position the work. DEFECT (credibility/presentation, and the promissory camera-ready language signals unfinished measurement).

(a) OVER-ASSERTION: 'LayerBudget achieves PPL ratio <= 1.03 at 4x on seven models from 7B to 72B' (false: Llama-2-13B = 1.11). 'LayerBudget ranks 1st among all token-compression methods' and 'it outperforms H2O, CAKE, SnapKV, D2O, and Ada-KV' at 'every configuration' (10 of 17 baselines are never shown; and in Table A1 eviction-only beats joint at Llama-2 3x). 'The optimal strategy is therefore to exhaust quantization headroom before evicting tokens' ('optimal' asserted; Table A1 shows quant-only beating the joint method at 6x). 'attention sparsity profiles calibrated at short context transfer to 32K tokens without recalibration' (inferred from PPL agreement; Gini is never measured at 32K). 'LayerBudget preserves Full KV accuracy across all compression ratios' on MMLU (only 2x and 4x are tested). 'Nearly all existing methods apply their strategy uniformly across layers' (contradicted one page later). (b) VAGUE REFERENT: 'These results validate the Gini stability finding from Section [REF]' -- 'these results' are long-context PPL ratios, which measure no Gini quantity at all. 'This is intrinsic to the byte budget' (Table A1 caption) -- 'this' has no clear antecedent among the four numbers just cited. 'the marginal-gain allocator absorbs both regimes' (abstract) -- 'absorbs' is undefined and is contradicted by Llama-2-13B at 1.56. 'The reduction generalizes' -- from n=2 models. 'the joint approach uses only 51%' (truncated, referent unrecoverable). (c) THING-VS-PROCESS CONFLATION: 'LayerBudget' is simultaneously the allocator, the profiling+allocation+selection+fill pipeline, the DynamicCache implementation and the vLLM block manager -- the paper needs a whole paragraph (Sec 3.4) to disambiguate 1 ms from 100-513 ms because of it. 'profiling' means both the once-per-model offline F(b) calibration and the per-input Gini extraction, and the '<3%' deployment-overhead claim depends on which. 'compression ratio' names both the requested setting and the achieved outcome. (d) FALSE PRECISION: 'reduces output distortion by 96%' in the abstract, from one model at one CR (the second model gives 90.5%), quoted to two significant figures with no n. 'PPL ratio 1.004 at 4x' on the 72B model -- four significant digits from 6 WikiText-2 chunks whose acknowledged std is ~2.3 PPL. 'greedy achieves 118-119%' -- three significant figures against an unnamed denominator. 'Pearson rho = 0.194' across ~22 TinyLlama layers with no CI or p-value. 'the mean absolute error ... is 3.1%' with no n. 'Decode latency remains within 3-5%' when the table spans +2.6% to +12.2%. NIAH values '93.3 / 86.7 / 73.3 / 46.7' are 1/15 or 1/30 granularity reported to one decimal. DEFECT in all four sweeps.

Thesis in one sentence: 'Allocating token count and KV bit-width jointly per layer, online, with a greedy marginal-gain rule, yields near-lossless KV cache compression at 2-4x across 7B-72B models.' Topic sentences map to the thesis in the Intro (KV cache is the memory bottleneck; two families exist; they are applied uniformly; quantize-first is better; sensitivity is per-layer), Method (problem formulation; coverage; fidelity; importance; two signals; greedy; theory), and most of Experiments. Paragraphs mapping to NEITHER the thesis nor their own topic sentence: (1) The ~500-word MoE-nD paragraph in Related Work -- its topic sentence promises positioning against concurrent work but its body is a head-to-head results table discussion, the introduction of a new method variant (LayerBudget-KV), and a baseline-fidelity disclaimer. Three different jobs, none of them 'related work'; the results belong in Sec 4 and the caveat in a limitation. (2) The 'Byte-CR Reconciliation' appendix -- its evidence (H2O at 6.02x, KIVI at 3.93x, LayerBudget at 3.04x) contradicts its own topic sentence ('the 2x inflation is fixed across methods'), and its conclusion is a promise to regenerate the table later. This is an erratum, not a section; delete the offending table and regenerate it instead. (3) The LayerBudget-KV appendix -- the topic sentence claims the variant's flat PPL 'is not solver degeneracy', but the paragraph's evidence (plan dumps differ across CR) establishes only that the plans differ, not that the flatness is meaningful; and the section ends by reporting the variant's NIAH collapse to 26.7%, which argues against including the variant at all. (4) The Sec 4.2 paragraph beginning 'These results validate the Gini stability finding' -- no evidence in the paragraph bears on Gini. (5) I cannot identify a topic sentence for the block that begins 'We identify the following limitations' -- it appears with no section heading, immediately after a sentence that ends mid-clause ('On LongBench (16 English tasks, Table~[REF]'), so the Analysis section and the Limitations section are fused. That fusion is itself the finding. DEFECT.

I have the LaTeX/text only, not a compiled PDF, so the three figures (ppl_scaling.pdf, allocation_heatmap.pdf, signal_curves.pdf) are UNVERIFIABLE as rendered -- I flag that explicitly. Two integrity problems are nonetheless visible from the captions and text. (1) Both mechanism figures are on the wrong model: 'Per-layer allocation at 2x-6x on TinyLlama' and 'Gini sparsity and sigmoid importance across layers. Weak correlation (rho=0.194)' are computed on TinyLlama-1.1B, which appears in NO results table -- the seven evaluated models are 7B-72B. The two figures that are supposed to show why the method works therefore illustrate a model whose behaviour is never validated, and the Intro's motivating statistic ('Gini ranges from 0.43 to 0.93 ... a 2.1x spread') comes from the same non-evaluated model. The rho=0.194 'complementary signals' argument, which justifies using two signals at all, is a single correlation on that one 1.1B model. (2) The right panel of the scaling figure is captioned 'LayerBudget (bold) outperforms all eviction methods and matches KIVI at 2-3x' -- 'matches' is the accurate word and it contradicts the paper's own 'ranks 1st' framing; a figure whose caption concedes a tie with the strongest baseline should not be supporting a first-place claim. DEFECT (figures unverifiable, plus a demonstrable model-mismatch between the mechanism figures and the evaluation).

(a) What the algorithm actually computes: Algorithm 1 initializes every layer at (n_min, 4 bits) and repeatedly applies the single (layer, action) maximizing delta[C(l,n_l) * F(b_l) * w_l] / delta[2 n_l H d b_l / 8], where C = (n_l/S)^(1-g_l) is a power-law fit to captured attention mass, F is a cosine similarity between FP16 and dequantized KV, and w_l is a fixed sigmoid in layer index. (b) Does it equal the object the theory names? Partly. The MCKP framing and the concavity argument are honest, and the paper correctly declines the (1-1/e) submodular bound with a specific reason (product objective, non-matroid action graph). But the object being maximized, Sum_l C*F*w, is never shown to be monotone in -- or even correlated with -- the object being measured (PPL, MMLU, NIAH). Only the C factor is validated (3.1% MAE against attention mass on one model); F is validated as a cosine similarity but never mapped to quality; w is a hand-set sigmoid with k=5, tau=0.3, neither derived nor ablated. There is no experiment showing the greedy allocation beats a random or uniform allocation at equal bytes under the same fill strategy, so the solver's value over its own action space is unmeasured. The '118-119%' figure that would speak to solver quality has no named denominator and, if the denominator were the MCKP optimum, would be impossible. (c) Semantics silently changed: TWO. (i) The importance term w_l is presented as a property of the model ('early layers are the primary quality bottleneck under eviction ... reversing the conventional assumption') but the paper's own LOO probe shows the direction reverses on Llama-2-13B and vanishes on Qwen2.5-14B. The solver is therefore run everywhere with a term whose sign is known to be wrong for at least one evaluated architecture -- and the resulting cell (Llama-2-13B, 1.11 at 4x / 1.56 at 6x) is the paper's worst. A per-layer importance prior that is empirically wrong for the architecture in question is a load-bearing assumption that is unjustified in the non-toy setting (gate item b). (ii) Mean-fill changes what 'eviction' means: evicted positions still participate in attention as a mean vector, so the K/V tensors the attention kernel consumes span S positions rather than n_l. The paper never states how this is realized -- materialized (in which case the reported byte savings are not realized) or broadcast from a single vector (in which case a custom kernel is required and is not described) -- and it simultaneously calls the alternative, zero-fill, 'the practical deployment setting'. The headline table is thus produced under a mechanism whose memory cost is unaccounted and whose deployability the authors implicitly deny. DEFECT.

Contributions as claimed, in order, with their isolating experiment and measured marginal effect. C1 'per-layer (n_l,b_l) allocation + quantize-first greedy solver' -- isolating experiment: Table A1 component analysis. Measured effect: Joint 1.00 vs Quant-only 1.00 (Mistral 3x, TIE); Joint 1.02 vs Quant-only 1.02 (Llama-2 3x, TIE, and Eviction-only 1.00 BEATS joint); Joint 3.23 vs Quant-only 1.00 (Mistral 6x, joint LOSES by 3.2x); Joint 45.09 vs Quant-only 1.01 (Llama-2 6x, joint LOSES by 45x). Marginal effect <= 0 in every measured cell. The sub-mechanism 'INT4/INT8 headroom' has its own isolating experiment (A3): {4,16} vs {4,8,16} differ by 0.01 in one of eight cells and are identical in the other seven -- the INT8 rung is worth nothing. The paper's own budget sweep further states that at 1.5-3.5x 'all signal variants are equivalent ... no tokens are evicted', i.e. across most of the claimed 2-4x envelope the method degenerates to uniform INT4 (= KIVI). C2 'inverted importance, +60-94% at 6x' -- isolating experiment: importance-direction ablation. Against the honest baseline (Flat/uniform, not the deliberately inverted Sigmoid), the effect at 4x is 1.010 -> 1.008 on Mistral (0.2%) and 1.067 -> 1.002 on Llama-2; the large gains appear only at 6x (1.734 -> 1.283; 5.94 -> 2.52), i.e. outside the operating envelope the paper claims. And the direction is Mistral-specific by the paper's own LOO probe. C3 'mean-fill, KL -96%' -- isolating experiment: mean-fill vs zero-fill. Measured effect: PPL 45.09 -> 1.13 on Llama-2 at 6x; KL 0.249 -> 0.009 and 0.6696 -> 0.0636. This is by far the largest measured effect in the paper, and it is billed THIRD. Its own control shows median-fill and random-fill are equivalent, so the transferable claim is 'do not zero-fill', which is a one-line implementation note, not a method. C4 '17 reimplemented baselines' -- no isolating experiment is applicable, but the reimplementations are unvalidated (SnapKV near chance on MMLU). C5 '16K-32K validation' -- supported, but only on PPL, and KIVI matches (1.008 vs 1.009 at Mistral 32K 4x). C6 '72B scaling' -- supported, and KIVI matches or beats it in every cell (1.00 flat vs 1.00/1.00/1.00/1.06; RULER 99 vs 98 at 2x). VERDICT: the ranking by measured marginal effect is the exact inverse of the abstract's ordering. The contribution billed first has a non-positive isolated effect; the contribution billed third carries the results and is not method-specific. Per the probe definition this is a FATAL credit-assignment defect; the honest fix is to demote the joint-allocation claim, not to argue for it. DEFECT.

(a) One-sentence contribution in this community's vocabulary: 'A training-free, online per-layer allocator that jointly chooses a token-retention budget and a KV quantization bit-width under a global memory budget, evaluated across seven 7B-72B models.' That sentence forms cleanly, so the paper is not mis-venued -- KV-cache compression is squarely NeurIPS / ICLR / MLSys efficient-inference territory, the baselines are this community's baselines, and the evaluation surfaces (WikiText-2 PPL, LongBench, RULER, NIAH, MMLU, GSM8K) are its standard ones. (b) Terms a PC member would have to look up, all author coinages: 'coverage law' (a power-law fit, not a law), 'fidelity constant F(b)', 'inverted importance', 'mean-fill', 'quantize first, evict last', 'the MoE-nD framing', 'LayerBudget-KV'. None is unreasonable, but none is standard, and 'coverage law' overstates a 3.1%-MAE empirical fit on one model. (c) No mechanism belongs to another community's conference; I would not forward this elsewhere on fit grounds. The one framing gap is the reverse: the systems half (vLLM block manager, TPOT, memory savings) is under-evaluated by MLSys standards -- no throughput, no batch-size-at-fixed-memory, and a measured speedup below 1x -- so an MLSys PC would find the systems claim unsupported while a NeurIPS PC finds the ML claim unsupported by the KIVI comparison. (d) Positioning currency is the real problem: the related work is written against 2024-2025 literature (H2O, SnapKV, PyramidKV, KIVI, KVQuant, MiniKV) plus two unreleased concurrent works the authors reimplemented themselves. The 2026 results that set the current bar in this exact sub-area -- RDKV (the same rate-distortion joint-allocation formulation), HqeKV (ACL 2026 Findings, public code), ThinKV, KVTC (ICLR 2026), STAR-KV (ICML 2026 Spotlight), DefensiveKV / Layer-DefensiveKV (ICLR 2026), PolyKV, KVCompose -- are absent entirely, as are LongBench-v2, InfiniteBench, SCBench and the effective-bits-per-token currency the field now reports. A paper whose claimed envelope is 2-4x, submitted into a field where published methods report 14-20x and <5% cache retention, has to explain that gap and does not. DEFECT (literature currency and unsupported systems claim, not mis-venuing).

(a) Expected metrics for this problem, marked: WikiText-2 / PG-19 PPL REPORTED (n=6 chunks, no CIs); LongBench-v1 REPORTED but the harness is broken (Full KV = 0.040-0.056); LongBench-v2 OMITTED (v1 is now considered dated); RULER 4K-128K REPORTED only once, at 4K, on one model (72B); InfiniteBench OMITTED; SCBench (the KV-cache-centric benchmark) OMITTED; NIAH REPORTED but at n=15-30 per cell and with a Full-KV score of 86.7% at only 4K on Mistral, indicating a misconfigured harness; MMLU REPORTED; GSM8K REPORTED (n=200, non-discriminating -- the method beats Full KV on 3 of 4 models); AIME / MATH-500 / GPQA / LiveCodeBench for the reasoning-model regime OMITTED entirely; effective bits per token OMITTED (the field's common currency, and the natural way to make this paper's CR comparable across methods); throughput (tokens/s), max batch size at fixed VRAM, TTFT, and peak memory at long context ALL OMITTED -- only TPOT overhead (+2.6% to +12.2%), prefill profiling overhead (+61-109%) and a footnote conceding speedup < 1x are given. (b) Do headline claims depend on an omitted metric? Yes, three. 'Ranks 1st among token-compression methods at memory-matched comparison' depends on a byte accounting that the paper's own tables show is inconsistent and on a memory-matched appendix that is cited but never presented. 'KV cache compression is most impactful at long context' plus the 32K claims rest on PPL alone, and the paper's own data shows PPL is a poor proxy there (H2O reports 83x PPL yet 0.056 on LongBench, higher than Full KV). The token-count-reduction advantage over KIVI -- the paper's only structural differentiator -- can only be cashed out in throughput or batch size, neither of which is measured, and the one systems number that is measured (speedup < 1x) points the wrong way. Any of these three could reverse the central claim. (c) Unmeasured terms inside the paper's own objective: the objective is Sum_l C(l,n_l) * F(b_l) * w_l, and the achieved value of that objective is never reported for any run; F is never mapped to any quality metric; w_l is never validated (indeed the LOO probe falsifies its direction on Llama-2-13B); and the '118-119%' solver-quality figure has no stated reference. (d) Workload regime vs claims: the claims are stated over long-context serving ('KV cache compression is most impactful at long context'; the motivating example is 70B at 8K needing 40 GB), but the headline table is WikiText-2 PPL at S=1024, the ablations are at S=512, NIAH is at 4096, LongBench at 4096, and only two models reach 32K on PPL alone. The evaluated regime does not match the regime the claims are stated over. DEFECT.
